segments.label: Trans-Canada Hwy, Bow Valley sector A
segments.connectivity_note: Splits two forest patches, each below grizzly's viable size; a full span reconnects them.

segments.label: US-191 — Trappers Point, Greater Yellowstone
segments.connectivity_note: Cuts the pronghorn's Path of the Pronghorn migration corridor between the Green River basin and summer range; a span reconnects the seasonal route.

segments.label: Snake River headwaters, Greater Yellowstone
segments.connectivity_note: A braided-river reach separating riparian willow patches used by moose and grizzly; a crossing restores movement across the valley floor.

segments.label: Interstate 15 — Monida Pass, High Divide
segments.connectivity_note: Four-lane interstate over the Continental Divide splitting Centennial Range forest from Big Hole grassland; a span rejoins two sub-viable elk patches.

segments.label: US-93 — Lost Trail Pass, Bitterroot Range
segments.connectivity_note: Highway on the Idaho–Montana divide fragmenting Bitterroot forest either side of the pass; a crossing links wolverine and lynx habitat across the ridgeline.

segments.label: Salmon River, Frank Church Wilderness
segments.connectivity_note: The River of No Return divides low-elevation winter range from north-slope forest; a crossing reconnects wintering elk and bighorn habitat.

segments.label: US-95 — Purcell Trench, Cabinet–Purcell
segments.connectivity_note: The Purcell Trench highway is the main barrier between the Cabinet and Purcell ranges' grizzly subpopulations; a span reconnects the two.

segments.label: BC-3 (Crowsnest) — Kootenay, Inland Rainforest
segments.connectivity_note: Provincial highway severing Selkirk inland-rainforest patches on the Kootenay Lake benches; a crossing rejoins mountain-caribou and grizzly range.

segments.label: US-2 — Marias Pass, Crown of the Continent
segments.connectivity_note: The highway along Glacier's southern boundary is a documented grizzly mortality corridor; a span reconnects park habitat with the Great Bear wildlands.

segments.label: BC-97 — Pine Pass, Peace River Break
segments.connectivity_note: Highway 97 through the Hart Ranges pinches the corridor at its narrowest point; a span holds open the last forested link across the Peace River Break.

segments.label: Peace River canyon, Peace River Break
segments.connectivity_note: The Peace River canyon splits boreal patches north and south; a crossing reconnects the constrained wildlife route through the break.

segments.label: Alaska Highway — Muskwa Ranges
segments.connectivity_note: The Alaska Highway threads the Muskwa Ranges, dividing intact boreal patches; a span keeps the Muskwa–Kechika movement network continuous.

segments.label: Kechika River, Muskwa–Kechika
segments.connectivity_note: The Kechika separates basin wetland from range-front forest; a crossing reconnects caribou and moose seasonal habitat.

segments.label: BC-37 (Cassiar) — Upper Liard Basin
segments.connectivity_note: The Stewart–Cassiar Highway fragments Liard Plateau boreal forest; a span reconnects lynx and caribou range across the corridor.

segments.label: Liard River, Upper Liard Basin
segments.connectivity_note: The Liard divides plateau wetland complexes; a crossing restores movement between riparian patches used by moose and bear.

segments.label: BC-37 (Stewart–Cassiar) — Sacred Headwaters
segments.connectivity_note: The highway crosses the Sacred Headwaters, splitting Spatsizi Plateau habitat; a span reconnects the Stikine–Skeena wildlife network.

segments.label: Stikine headwaters, Spatsizi Plateau
segments.connectivity_note: Headwater channels divide subalpine range on the plateau; a crossing rejoins caribou calving and summer habitat.

segments.label: Canol Road — Mackenzie Mountains
segments.connectivity_note: The remote Canol Road breaks the Selwyn–Mackenzie forest belt; even a light-traffic corridor fragments habitat, and a span reconnects it.

segments.label: South Nahanni headwaters, Mackenzie Mtns
segments.connectivity_note: Headwaters of the South Nahanni separate range-front forest from valley wetland; a crossing reconnects Dall sheep and moose habitat.
